edits.label: Time to first signed contract for the paid diagnostic
edits.words: Set "Time to first signed contract for the paid diagnostic" to between 6 and 12 months.

facts.text: Olumi's what-if for 'Time from starting the offer to the first signed customer contract', not their figure: 0.25 to 12 months. Basis: Shared timing input for either a product or service offer. An accessible buyer might sign within weeks, while finding an enterprise sponsor and clearing procurement could take many months. No supplied typical rate fits Paul's unspecified offer and pipeline. The band is a replaceable what-if conditional on eventually making a sale; no sale or a longer wait remains possible.

Olumi's what-if for 'Time to first signed contract for consulting', not their figure: 0.25 to 12 months. Basis: Replaceable what-if spanning a sale to an accessible buyer within weeks through a lengthy enterprise prospecting and procurement process. Paul supplied no pipeline or offer-readiness information, and no library rate fits this consulting sale. The same exploratory band is used for the diagnostic because its smaller scope does not establish faster procurement. Conditional on a sale occurring; no sale and longer waits are not represented by this finite interval.

Olumi's what-if for 'Time from first signed contract to first customer payment', not their figure: 0 to 6 months. Basis: Replaceable what-if for unspecified service payment terms: a deposit can arrive at signing, whereas payment after delivery can require several months of work followed by an invoice-payment period. Six months allows a substantial delivery-and-collection cycle without asserting that it is typical. No applicable library rate or customer terms were supplied. This is the planned delay; unexpected lateness is represented separately.

Olumi's what-if for 'Consulting contract-to-payment delay', not their figure: 0 to 6 months. Basis: Replaceable what-if covering an immediate deposit, milestone billing, or several months of delivery followed by collection. Consulting scope and terms are unknown, so no central estimate is supported and longer arrangements remain possible. No library rate fits. Unlike the explicitly upfront-paid diagnostic, broader consulting has no proposed upfront-payment requirement. Unexpected payment slippage is excluded here to avoid counting it twice.

Olumi's what-if for 'Paid diagnostic contract-to-payment delay', not their figure: 0 to 0.5 months. Basis: An illustrative what-if for an explicitly upfront-paid diagnostic: cash may arrive at signing or after a short administrative delay. This is not a published rate and applies only if the buyer accepts and follows upfront-payment terms; late payment remains a separate risk.

Olumi's what-if for 'Enterprise service engagements completed within the exploration window', not their figure: 0 to 6 engagements. Basis: Replaceable small-scale what-if for the proposed six-month exploration: from no completed enterprise work to six engagements, averaging one completion per month. This tests a modest service launch alongside the startup rather than assuming an established consulting operation. Neither demand nor capacity is known; six is a scenario endpoint, not an evidenced capacity ceiling. No library rate fits.

Olumi's what-if for 'Enterprise consulting engagements completed within the exploration window', not their figure: 0 to 6 engagements. Basis: Replaceable what-if for a small consulting launch over the proposed six months: zero completions if sales or delivery do not materialise, up to six if relatively bounded engagements can be sold and delivered. One completion per month on average is an exploratory workload, not a demand forecast or capacity estimate. No library rate applies. The diagnostic receives the same band because neither its demand nor a delivery-capacity advantage is established.

Olumi's what-if for 'Enterprise diagnostics completed within the exploration window', not their figure: 0 to 6 engagements. Basis: Replaceable what-if for a small six-month diagnostic test, spanning no completed sales to six completions. A fixed scope could limit delivery work, but its actual size, pipeline and staffing are unknown; there is no basis for a higher volume band than consulting. This is an exploratory scale, not calibrated demand or a hard capacity ceiling. No library rate fits.

Olumi's what-if for 'Additional qualified enterprise opportunities per completed engagement', not their figure: 0% to 100% (opportunity per engagement). Basis: Replaceable, deliberately uninformative what-if: none through all completed engagements might reveal one genuinely additional qualified opportunity. Expressed as opportunities per engagement, equivalent to the previous percentage under the provisional maximum of one opportunity per engagement. Paul has supplied no further-offering definition, buyer overlap or customer evidence that would justify excluding either endpoint or choosing a likely value. SaaS trial conversion and opportunity win rates measure different mechanisms and do not apply. This is a sensitivity range, not an empirical probability estimate.

Olumi's what-if for 'Additional qualified enterprise opportunities per completed consulting engagement', not their figure: 0% to 100% (opportunity per engagement). Basis: Replaceable sensitivity range from no consulting engagements yielding a further qualified opportunity to all yielding one. Expressed as opportunities per engagement, equivalent to the previous percentage under the provisional maximum of one opportunity per engagement. Consulting could reveal unmet needs, but bespoke-work buyers might have no further relevant purchase. No evidence supports a narrower band or a central value; no library rate measures this additionality mechanism. The diagnostic uses the same band because its discovery focus alone establishes no conversion advantage.

Olumi's what-if for 'Additional qualified enterprise opportunities per completed diagnostic', not their figure: 0% to 100% (opportunity per engagement). Basis: Replaceable sensitivity range allowing none through all diagnostics to yield one additional qualified opportunity. Expressed as opportunities per engagement, equivalent to the previous percentage under the provisional maximum of one opportunity per engagement. A diagnostic deliberately investigates needs, but that does not establish budget, buying authority, product fit or additionality. No applicable library benchmark or customer evidence supports narrowing the range or assigning a likely value. Its band therefore matches consulting's without claiming equal underlying conversion rates.

Olumi's what-if for 'Chance of customer payment slippage during the exploration window', not their figure: 10% to 60%. Basis: Replaceable stress-test chance of payment slippage at least once over the entire proposed six-month window, not a monthly rate. The broad 10–60% band explores occasional through fairly common administrative or dispute-related delays in a new service relationship. No applicable library rate, customer payment history or calibrated probability is available; this is conditional on having a payment due.

Olumi's what-if for 'Additional collection delay when payment slippage occurs', not their figure: 0.25 to 3 months. Basis: Replaceable what-if for extra delay beyond agreed terms: roughly a week for routine administration through three months for repeated follow-up or a dispute. No library benchmark or customer evidence fits. This sizes lateness only, not the planned delivery or invoice-payment period; non-payment and longer disputes are not represented.

Olumi's what-if for 'Chance consulting displaces other startup work during the exploration window', not their figure: 20% to 80%. Basis: Replaceable stress-test chance of displacement at least once across the whole proposed six-month window, conditional on taking consulting work. Adding bespoke delivery alongside an existing startup can compete for attention, but dedicated staffing could substantially reduce that competition. The wide 20–80% band reflects these unknown arrangements, not a measured startup base rate; no library rate fits.

Olumi's what-if for 'Enterprise engagement multiplier when consulting displaces other startup work', not their figure: 0.5 to 1.5. Basis: Replaceable what-if retaining the existing risk's unknown direction on service-engagement volume: delivery overload could halve completions, while shifting time away from the other offering toward consulting could increase them by half. These are exploratory workload perturbations, not empirical effects. No staffing or capacity data or applicable library rate exists. This multiplier does not measure the harm to the other offering itself.

Olumi's what-if for 'Time to first signed product contract', not their figure: 0.25 to 12 months. Basis: A provisional what-if spanning an accessible buyer able to purchase within weeks through many months of finding a sponsor and clearing enterprise procurement. Product readiness, pricing and pipeline are unknown. No applicable checked typical rate supports a narrower range or a timing advantage over consulting, so the exploratory band matches consulting's. Conditional on a sale occurring; no sale and waits beyond the band remain possible.

Olumi's what-if for 'Product contract-to-payment delay', not their figure: 0 to 6 months. Basis: A replaceable what-if covering payment at signing through a substantial enterprise acceptance and collection cycle. Paul has not described the product's billing or acceptance terms. The wide band matches the unspecified consulting terms rather than assuming product sales collect faster or slower. No applicable checked typical rate is available. Unexpected payment slippage remains separate.

facts.value: about 13% (about 16% without Olumi's suggested risk assumption 'Customer payment arrives later than agreed')
facts.text: If Olumi's estimates hold, the chance that 'Add consulting services to the AI startup' meets 'Generate revenue as quickly as possible', in this model on current information. Without Olumi's suggested risk assumption 'Customer payment arrives later than agreed', which is Olumi's own hypothesis and a different model from this one, the chance is about 16%. It rests on Olumi's reading of the aim and Olumi's proposed target (at most 3 months), not yet confirmed by them. It rests on Olumi's what-if ranges for 'Time to first signed contract for consulting' (0.25 to 12 months), 'Consulting contract-to-payment delay' (0 to 6 months), 'Chance of customer payment slippage during the exploration window' (10% to 60%), 'Additional collection delay when payment slippage occurs' (0.25 to 3 months). It rests on Olumi's proposed figures for 'Customer payment arrives later than agreed', not yet confirmed by them. It rests on: Read revenue urgency initially as elapsed time from starting the offer to receiving the first customer payment. It leaves out: First-payment timing does not cover revenue size, profit, repeatability, delivery burden or revenue forgone from other startup work.

facts.value: about 55% (about 58% without Olumi's suggested risk assumption 'Consulting commitments displace work on the startup's other offering')
facts.text: If Olumi's estimates hold, the chance that 'Add consulting services to the AI startup' meets 'Create additional opportunities to sell the product', in this model on current information. Without Olumi's suggested risk assumption 'Consulting commitments displace work on the startup's other offering', which is Olumi's own hypothesis and a different model from this one, the chance is about 58%. It rests on Olumi's reading of the aim and Olumi's proposed target (at least 1 opportunity), not yet confirmed by them. It rests on Olumi's what-if ranges for 'Enterprise consulting engagements completed within the exploration window' (0 to 6 engagements), 'Additional qualified enterprise opportunities per completed consulting engagement' (0% to 100% (opportunity per engagement)), 'Chance consulting displaces other startup work during the exploration window' (20% to 80%), 'Enterprise engagement multiplier when consulting displaces other startup work' (0.5 to 1.5). It rests on Olumi's proposed figures for 'Consulting commitments displace work on the startup's other offering', 'Exploration window', not yet confirmed by them. It rests on: Count a further product sales opportunity only when an enterprise buyer has an identified product need, a buying contact and an agreed next sales step, and the opportunity would not otherwise have existed. Initially count at most one per completed service engagement. It leaves out: The opportunity count covers service-generated product opportunities, not opportunities from direct product selling, eventual wins, sales value, opportunities arising before service completion, or product opportunities lost through displaced selling effort.
